response.consequence: The event-type editor unmounts and remounts after a save or refetch. Unsaved form state, the current tab and the ref handle are lost. The editor flickers blank, and the data can keep resetting and refetching.
response.explanation: The dependency array of the cleanup-only useEffect gained `eventTypeQueryData`. The cleanup, which calls `invalidateQueries` and `resetQueries`, used to run only on unmount or when `id` changed. It now also runs each time `eventTypeQueryData` gets a new reference. That happens after a successful update, a background refetch, or a window-focus refetch. `resetQueries` clears the cached data, so `useAtomsEventTypeById` returns undefined. The wrapper then hits `if (!eventTypeQueryData) return null` and unmounts the whole EventType form until the refetch completes. The cleanup runs again on the next data change, so the reset can repeat.
response.title: Effect cleanup now fires on every data change and resets the event-type query

response.consequence: A host can see a Confirm button on pending bookings that the old logic hid, for example when the payment app is enabled and no payment record exists. The old paid-booking confirm path is also lost.
response.explanation: The old condition was `(isPending && !paymentAppData.enabled) || (paymentAppData.enabled && !!price && booking.paid)`. The refactor passes `showPendingPayment = enabled && payment.length && !booking.paid` into getPendingActions (bookingActions.ts:51), which checks `(isPending && !showPendingPayment) || (showPendingPayment && booking.paid)`. The second clause can never be true, because showPendingPayment already requires `!booking.paid`. The first clause now also shows Confirm for a pending booking when the payment app is enabled but `payment.length` is 0 or the booking is paid. The old code hid Confirm whenever the payment app was enabled and the booking was not paid.
